messages:
zoe: FYI I'm seeing a bunch of edge-api targets get removed from the ALB this morning — target state flips to UNUSED after failing health checks repeatedly.
sam: Which health path does the ALB call? Any 5xxs in the pod logs?
zoe: ALB -> GET /healthz (expect 200). App logs show 500s/503s for /healthz right after a new pod starts. Seems correlated with new pods and scale-ups.
matt: Could be the sidecar/proxy not proxying yet while the app initializes DB/pool. How is readiness configured today?
zoe: Current readinessProbe:
```
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 10
  failureThreshold: 3
```
julia: That initialDelay is pretty aggressive if the app needs to warm DB pools or run quick migrations. ALB health settings matter too.
kevin: ALB health config on the ingress is: healthcheck-path=/healthz, interval=10, timeout=5, unhealthy-threshold=2 — so ALB will mark target unhealthy fast if it takes >5s to respond.
sam: Right — combine kube readiness failing + ALB timeout leads to endpoints being removed and ALB deregistering the pod, causing 503s to users.
zoe: Repro I ran locally:
```
kubectl scale deploy/edge-api --replicas=3
# new pod logs
"initializing connection pool..."  (takes ~12s)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://<pod-ip>/healthz
# first 2-3 calls = 500, then 200
```
matt: Proposed fixes:
- bump readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 20 and failureThreshold to 8 for now
- increase ALB healthcheck timeout to 10 and unhealthy-threshold to 3
- add app-level warmup: /ready returns 200 only after pools are primed
- consider slow_start.duration_seconds on target group to smooth traffic
julia: Also add annotation to delay deregistration: `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/deregistration-delay.timeout_seconds: "60"` so ALB doesn't evict immediately on transient failures.
kevin: We can set `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/target-group-attributes: slow_start.duration_seconds=30` too.
sam: Testing plan: change readiness in staging, roll a single AZ, monitor ALB target health in AWS console and logs.
infra-bot: deployment edge-api/staging rolled by zoe at 2026-03-18T09:12:30Z (canary)
zoe: Staging canary results: new pod remained InService in ALB after warmup hook fired; no early deregisters. /healthz returned 200 once pool ready.
sam: Nice. Follow-ups:
- schedule prod tweak during next maintenance (prod readiness -> initialDelay 15 / period 10 / failureThreshold 6)
- apply ALB annotation changes (timeout 10s / unhealthy-threshold 3 / deregistration-delay 60s)
- implement lightweight /ready that flips only when pool is warm
- add alert for "Target deregistered" events in infra monitoring
matt: I'll add a short runbook snippet in eng-infra playbook: how to triage ALB deregister (curl pod /healthz, describe endpoints, check targetHealth on AWS, inspect ingress annotations).
julia: I'll own the runbook. Can someone open the infra ticket for the prod rollout? I'll also add the ingress annotations PR template.
kevin: I'll draft the prod-change PR and set up the rollout window, assign to sam for execution.
zoe: Great — thanks team. Good to confirm this was probe/warmup mismatch and not conntrack/NAT. :relieved:
sam: Marking this thread as resolved for now; reopen if prod shows issues.
